test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 17th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Besides banks, the other formal major source of cheap credit in rural areas, are __________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Cooperative Societies.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Cooperative societies are the other major source of low-cost finance in rural areas.
 
• Forms of cooperative societies are farmers cooperatives, weavers cooperatives, industrial workers cooperatives, Credit Cooperative Society, Consumer Cooperative Society, Producer Cooperative Societies, Marketing Cooperative Society, Housing Cooperative Society.
 
• Cooperative Societies are formed for the mutual benefit of its members. Hence, the Credit Cooperative Society provides low-cost finance or cheap credit to its members at very nominal rate of interest. 
 
• Example of Credit Cooperative Society - **Krishak Cooperative**
 
• Krishak Cooperative provides loans for construction of houses, fishery loans, loans for agricultural trade and cultivation, loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, and loans for a variety of other expenses. 
 
• The Cooperative also obtains a large loan from the bank, with these deposits from their members as collateral.
 
• Loans to members are given from these funds.
 
• Another round of lending can take place, once these loans are repaid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Other features of Cooperative Society are

 
• It needs to be registered mandatorily under Societies Registration Act, 1860, or the Cooperative Societies Act, 1912.
 
• There shall be at least 7 members with a draft of Memorandum of Association to register a Cooperative Society.
 
• It is governed by a managing committee that is elected democratically by its members.
 
• Audits are performed in cooperative societies, hence it is managed professionally.
 
• Its formation and participation of members are voluntary by nature.
 
• It is mutually beneficial to members of low and middle-income groups.
 
• Reduced financial risk.
